children.text: Nara states that she must let something simmer “for about five hours”, serving as a form of ragebait that is likely to garner engagement. With the first tag of her caption in this video being “#easyrecipe”, a process that involves a single step where something must simmer for five hours is completely contradictory. The comments on this video are filled with viewers calling Nara out for how long her recipes take, with many saying things like “dinner will be ready in 2 days” and “20 hour instant ramen”. This serves as a successful example of ragebait, where Nara’s choice was intentional and struck up more engagement on her video.

Throughout her cooking process, Nara can be seen wearing an elaborate outfit that she does not provide any context or commentary for. In a typical at-home cooking setting, high fashion is not fitting and serves no logical purpose. Nara’s choice to put on such an outfit while she works through a complicated recipe is an avenue to strike up engagement with the pure visual irony that it exudes. No viewer expects to see Nara wearing such an outfit while cooking in the comfort of her own home, so this serves as a popular point of engagement in the comment section. Users question the need for this level of fashion, ultimately uplifting the circulation of this video.

Nara utilizes voice-over as an affordance in her content, allowing her to narrate her video with a walkthrough of her recipe and make it clear to viewers. However, she brings her own nuance to it with a whispery and slightly monotone delivery. As she walks through her complicated recipe, she very often notes how long certain points of the process will take: “let that simmer for about 5 hours”, “put it in my dehydrator for about 16 hours”. Her delivery of these absurd times with a gentle and ‘unbothered’ tone serves yet another method to strike engagement from viewers, and acts as a highly effective use of voiceovers as an affordance.

Nara introduces the recipe that she is making as a recreation of Top Ramen, a widely known meal that is most praised for its convenience and quickness. This likely grabs the attention of viewers because of how well-known Top Ramen is. However, Nara turns this previously fast meal into a long, complicated, and labor-intensive process that ends up taking her over 16 hours. Hooking viewers with the mention of a dish that many are familiar with and then flipping it into such an elaborate recipe is a clear method to stir more engagement from annoyed and confused users, striking viewers and garnering more attention.

Nara’s use of certain hashtags in the caption of her video brings her intentions to light and simultaneously brings the video better exposure and circulation. With the use of hashtags being an affordance on TikTok’s platform, influencers will tag their content with phrases that attract their desired audience. Nara’s decision to put “#easyrecipe” as a tag will bring attention from viewers looking for easy recipes. However, being met with an elaborate recipe such as Nara’s, viewers will look at the video in a negative light because it truly is the opposite of easy. This is another way Nara strikes up engagement, because annoyed users will question her understanding of what an easy recipe really is.
